findings.diagnosis: The prompt underestimates cuts that leave an apparent standalone claim (an incomplete predicate, a subject without its verb/object, or a list-item that reads like an assertion). Ask at each marker: “If the left fragment were read alone, would it assert a complete fact or assignment that the remainder could negate, reassign, or complete?” If yes, treat the marker as very risky (raise contra sharply and/or set cohesion very low).
findings.evidence: 7 cases (en_us_1591, en_us_1427, en_us_1593, en_us_1514, en_us_608, en_us_877, en_us_1192). In each, the policy kept cuts that left a subject or enumerated item dangling (e.g. a person + ordinal, a subject without its predicate, or a verb split from its object) — fragments that the remainder either completes or contradicts, and which the measured H shows should have been penalized heavily.

edit.text: Add rule: At every marker explicitly test for 'standalone-claim risk' — would the left chunk, read alone, assert a definite fact (a subject with an implied outcome, an item+ordinal/amount, or a verb that looks finished)? If yes, raise contra toward 1.0 and/or set cohesion near 0. This is distinct from mere awkwardness: it's when the right-hand material is required to make the left-hand statement truthful or unambiguous.

findings.diagnosis: The prompt fails to treat boundaries inside enumerations or mapped lists (assignments across multiple antecedents) as especially dangerous. Ask: “Does the left fragment assign an element, ordinal, quantity, or role within a larger list that the remainder will distribute or remap (the kind of construction that yields 'respectively' or paired assignments)?” If yes, increase contra because the left fragment is likely misleading when isolated.
findings.evidence: 3 cases (en_us_1591, en_us_1192, en_us_1514). In these examples the policy kept cuts that isolated an item plus an ordinal/quantity or split a list mapping, producing a fragment that asserts a concrete assignment that the following text redistributes — the measured contra and low H confirm these cuts are harmful.

edit.text: Add rule: For enumerations/mapped lists, explicitly flag cuts that isolate one list element together with an ordinal/quantity/role. Such fragments commonly become false or misleading when read alone because the remainder completes the mapping (e.g. multiple subjects matched to multiple ordinals). Treat these markers as high-contra and low-cohesion.
